metadata.title: Calvin Ridley - Remains limited at practice
metadata.description: Ridley (hip) was limited at practice Thursday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: The same applies applies to Wednesday's session, giving the wideout one more chance to up his participation level ahead of Sunday's game against the Bengals. So far this season, Ridley has recorded just five catches (on 10 targets) for 81 yards in six games, a pace that has kept him off the fantasy radar thus far.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley (hip) limited participant Thursday
metadata.description: Calvin Ridley (hip) was a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran was limited for another practice on Thursday, as he's still dealing with a hip issue of some kind. We should know more about his official status for Week 8 after practice on Friday.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley (hip) limited in practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Calvin Ridley was limited in practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Ridley remains off the fantasy radar when he is healthy.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley - Limited in Wednesday's session
metadata.description: Ridley (hip) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Ridley sat out the Titans' final two practices of Week 7 before sitting out an eventual 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday, but he was able to take a step forward in terms of activity for the start of Week 8 prep. If the veteran receiver is able to upgrade to full participation Thursday and/or Friday, he should be in line to suit up this weekend versus the Bengals. Before sitting out against the Browns, Ridley had put together a 5-81-0 receiving line on 10 targets through the Titans' first six games.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley - Returns to practice
metadata.description: Ridley (hip) returned to practice Wednesday, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Ridley was inactive for this past Sunday's game against the Browns after not practicing Thursday or Friday, but the wideout's presence for Wednesday's session offers hope that he may be available this weekend against the Bengals. The Titans' upcoming practice report will reveal Ridley's official participation level in his return to the practice field.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley Returns to Practice on Wednesday
metadata.description: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley (hip) returned to practice on Wednesday after missing the Week 7 loss on Sunday to the Cleveland Browns, according to Turron Davenport of ESPN. Ridley's return for the first practice of Week 8 preparation is a good sign, but it will not guarantee his return this Sunday on the road against the Cincinnati Bengals. The 31-year-old might be worth a look as a WR4/flex option in deeper fantasy leagues this weekend if he returns, but only if rookie first-rounder Carnell Tate (shoulder) does not play. Tate apparently picked up a shoulder injury on Sunday and was unable to practice on Wednesday. Ridley has done very little so far in 2026 in six games in his third year in Tennessee, catching only five of his 10 targets for 81 yards (16.2 yards per catch) without finding the end zone. After his slow start to his eighth year in the NFL, Ridley is rostered in only 1% of Yahoo leagues with Week 8 approaching.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley (hip) officially inactive for Week 7
metadata.description: Titans WR Calvin Ridley (hip) is officially inactive for a Week 7 matchup with the Browns.
metadata.analysis: Ridley was tagged as questionable as he dealt with a hip injury that lingered throughout the week. His absence will likely open up some playing time for a few depth wide receivers on the roster.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley - Inactive in Week 7
metadata.description: Ridley (hip) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Browns.
metadata.analysis: Ridley opened Week 7 prep with a limited session Wednesday due to a hip injury, but he followed it up with back-to-back DNPs, leaving him questionable ahead of the weekend. With inactive status confirmed Sunday, Ridley will cede his role to some combination of Wan'Dale Robinson, Elic Ayomanor, Chimere Dike and K.J. Osborn behind top WR Carnell Tate. Ridley's next chance for game action is Sunday, Nov. 1, at Cincinnati.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley Inactive With Hip Injury in Week 7
metadata.description: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley (hip) is inactive for Sunday's Week 7 matchup against the Cleveland Browns, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter, a move that puts Elic Ayomanor on the radar in deeper fantasy leagues only. Ridley was questionable after practicing on a limited basis Wednesday before sitting out Thursday and Friday. The veteran has caught just five of 10 targets for 81 yards on the season and played 28 of Tennessee's 46 offensive snaps in Week 6, matching Ayomanor's workload. Ayomanor could see considerably more playing time alongside Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson, but he has drawn only 14 targets through six games, catching seven passes for 133 yards and a touchdown. That limited involvement in the passing game makes him difficult to trust in standard-sized leagues.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley is Considered Questionable for Week 7
metadata.description: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley (hip) is listed as questionable ahead of the Week 7 matchup against the Cleveland Browns. Ridley was limited in practice to start the week, but then he didn't practice at all on Thursday or Friday. When healthy, Ridley has been a non-factor in this offense so far. Through six games, Ridley has recorded five receptions with 81 receiving yards and zero touchdowns. The absence of the 31-year-old wideout would likely mean that Elic Ayomanor would slide into the No. 3 wideout role. Neither player has done enough this season to warrant starting in any fantasy lineups in Week 7.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley (hip) listed questionable for Sunday
metadata.description: Calvin Ridley (hip) is listed questionable for Sunday's game against the Cleveland Cavaliers.
metadata.analysis: The veteran has been dealing with a hip injury throughout practice this week and will be questionable to play on Sunday as a result. His potential absence wouldn't carry much weight from a fantasy perspective, however.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley - Listed questionable for Sunday
metadata.description: Ridley (hip) will not practice Friday and is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Cleveland, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Ridley and Elic Ayomanor have been splitting WR snaps alongside No. 1 receiver Carnell Tate and slot man Wan'Dale Robinson. If Ridley were to miss Sunday's game, Ayomanor presumably would take on more playing time.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley - Trending in wrong direction
metadata.description: Ridley (hip) didn't practice Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Ridley is trending in the wrong direction, as he was unable to practice Thursday after being listed as limited Wednesday. Even if Ridley recovers in time to face the Browns on Sunday, he remains a non-factor for fantasy purposes, having caught only five passes through six games while dropping to fourth on Tennessee's wide receiver depth chart.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley (hip) listed as limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Calvin Ridley (hip) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Ridley is managing a hip issue and was relegated to a limited role at practice on Wednesday as a result. It remains to be seen if he will have an injury designation going into Week 7, but either way he remains off of the fantasy radar at this point.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley - Limited practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Ridley (hip) was a limited participant in practice Wednesday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site  reports.
metadata.analysis: The veteran is dealing with a hip issue but was able to get some work in during the first practice session of the week.  Ridley's status will come into focus in the coming days before the Titans release their final injury report ahead of the Week 7 game against the Browns.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley - Held without catch again
metadata.description: Ridley failed to haul in either of his two targets during the Titans' 26-20 win over the Colts on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Tennessee captured its first win of the season, although most of the credit can go to the defense and special teams, seeing as Cam Ward passed for only 102 yards (with 70 of those yards going to rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate). It was the third time in six games that Ridley failed to log a catch, and the veteran wideout has only five catches on 10 targets for 81 yards this season. He carries very little upside heading into a Week 7 home tilt against the Browns on Oct. 25.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley - Two snags in loss
metadata.description: Ridley caught two of three targets for 33 yards during Sunday's 26-3 loss to the Texans.
metadata.analysis: Ridley was limited to two or fewer catches for the fifth straight game to open the regular season, and he has yet to exceed 35 receiving yards in a contest this year. The wide receiver has reeled in five of eight targets for 81 yards over five contests this season, and he'll continue to have a rather low floor from a fantasy perspective in Week 6 against the Colts.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley totals 33 yards Sunday
metadata.description: Calvin Ridley caught 2-of-3 targets for 33 yards in the Titans 26-3 loss against the Texans.
metadata.analysis: Ridley remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley is Nearly Impossible to Trust in Week 5
metadata.description: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley has done almost nothing on offense through the first four games of the season. Heading into Week 5, Ridley has recorded three of his five targets for 48 yards and zero touchdowns. He'll now draw a tough matchup against the Houston Texans defense in Week 5. It's clear that Ridley isn't going to be a big part of the offense with Carnell Tate (back) and Wan'Dale Robinson being the primary options in the passing game. Ridley is probably worth holding in deep leagues, but he's not someone that should be trusted in starting lineups right now.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley - Just one catch in Week 4 loss
metadata.description: Ridley caught one pass on two targets for 13 yards during Sunday's 24-18 loss to the Ravens.
metadata.analysis: Ridley and the rest of the Titans pass catchers took a back seat to rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate, who turned 12 of his targets from Cam Ward into nine catches for 145 yards. Ridley was on the field for 30 of Tennessee's 64 offensive snaps (46.9 percent), which was fewer than Tate (54), Wan'Dale Robinson (43) and Elic Ayomanor (40). Ridley is off to a slow start to the 2026 season, accumulating only three catches (on five targets) for 48 yards through four games. The Titans head home for Week 5 against the Texans, whose secondary was torched by CeeDee Lamb in a Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley - Logs lesser role in Week 3 loss
metadata.description: Ridley didn't catch his only target Sunday in a loss to the Giants.
metadata.analysis: For the first time this season, Ridley was not among the Titans' top three wideouts in terms of offensive snaps. Carnell Tate (53 snaps) led the WR corps in that category, with Elic Ayomanor (48 snaps) and Wan'Dale Robinson (38 snaps) also both ahead of Ridley (20 snaps). That could be an indication that Tennessee is turning toward the younger Ayomanor over the veteran Ridley, who has caught just two passes for 35 yards through three contests on the campaign.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley catchless in loss Sunday
metadata.description: Calvin Ridley failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 12-7 loss to the New York Giants.
metadata.analysis: Ridley was a complete non-factor on Sunday, failing to record even a single catch in the team's loss to the Giants. He should not be considered a relevant fantasy option in any league formats moving forward.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley - Catches first passes of 2026
metadata.description: Ridley caught both of his targets for 35 yards during the Titans' 24-20 loss to the Eagles on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Ridley didn't see a target from Cam Ward during the Titans' Week 1 loss to the Jets. The veteran wide receiver finally got involved offensively with catches of 25 and 10 yards in the third quarter as part of a 12-play, 69-yard drive that ended with a one-yard touchdown scramble by Ward. Ridley was listed as a starter alongside Carnell Tate and Elic Ayomanor, and Ridley's 33 snaps on offense were second-most among Titans wide receivers behind Tate (40). Up next for Ridley and the Titans is a Week 3 road tilt against the Giants.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley goes for 35 yards in Week 2
metadata.description: Calvin Ridley caught both of his targets for 35 yards in a 24-20 loss to the Eagles in Week 2.
metadata.analysis: Ridley bounced back after not drawing a target in Week 1 but it was still a quiet performance for the veteran receiver. The Titans' passing game has not been very explosive through two games, which is making their pass-catchers hard to trust. Ridley will not be a strong fantasy option heading into Week 3 against the Giants.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley - Zero targets in Week 1 loss
metadata.description: Ridley played 32 offensive snaps and did not show up in the box score otherwise during the Titans' 23-10 loss to the Jets on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Ridley had the third-most snaps among Titans wide receivers behind Carnell Tate (44) and Wan'Dale Robinson (41), though Ridley didn't end up seeing a single target from quarterback Cam Ward during Sunday's loss. Ridley restructured his contract in mid-March after playing in only seven regular-season games in 2025, but it looks like the veteran wide receiver might be an afterthought in the Titans' offense. He'll look for better results in Tennessee's Week 2 clash against Philadelphia on Sept. 20.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley not targeted in Week 1
metadata.description: Calvin Ridley was not targeted in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: Ridley was on the field but did not record any stats in the lopsided loss to New York. The entire Titans offense struggled in the contest, but Ridley's lack of participation is still highly concerning going forward. He can be cut in shallow leagues heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Eagles.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley Holds Minimal Upside in Week 1 Despite Path to Starting Role
metadata.description: After dealing with a hamstring injury and a broken fibula that limited him to just seven games in 2025, wide receiver Calvin Ridley enters the 2026 campaign healthy and as a starter for the Tennessee Titans. The Titans take on the New York Jets in Week 1. Ridley will play alongside fellow wideouts Wan'Dale Robinson and Carnell Tate (rookie), as well as tight end Gunnar Helm, as he looks to establish himself as a top target for quarterback Cam Ward in the passing game. The 31-year-old Ridley recorded just 17 receptions for 303 yards and zero touchdowns during his injury-plagued 2025 campaign, but the veteran has amassed 405 catches for 5,678 yards and 40 touchdowns throughout his career. Ridley is currently rostered in just 4% of Yahoo leagues right now and ranks as RotoBaller's No. 80 wide receiver (half-PPR) in Week 1. It is safe to keep Ridley out of lineups for Week 1, but his situation is worth monitoring.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley - Experienced option in young WR room
metadata.description: Ridley is among the five wide receivers on the Titans' initial 53-man roster.
metadata.analysis: Tennessee heads into the season with Carnell Tate (undisclosed), Wan'Dale Robinson (head), Ridley, Chimere Dike and Elic Ayomanor at wide receiver. Of those five players, only Robinson and Ridley have more than one year of NFL experience. Ridley was the team's No. 1 receiver in the early part of last season but finished the year with just 303 receiving yards in seven games, as he missed time due to a hamstring injury and then fractured his fibula. Having recovered from those injuries, the 31-year-old Ridley is in contention for a starting role on the outside opposite Tate, with Robinson likely to work primarily out of the slot.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley - Logs one catch in preseason opener
metadata.description: Ridley caught his only target for 18 yards in Thursday's preseason win over San Francisco.
metadata.analysis: Ridley started the contest but was on the field for only the Titans' first drive, logging seven total offensive snaps. The veteran wideout appears healthy after playing in only seven games last season due to injuries, the last of which was a broken fibula he suffered in Week 11 that forced him to IR for the remainder of the campaign. Ridley looks to be set as Tennessee's No. 3 wide receiver this season behind first-round rookie Carnell Tate (undisclosed) and free-agent signing Wan'Dale Robinson, and the health of the Titans' passing game will largely depend on the growth (or lack thereof) of sophomore QB Cam Ward.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley Makes His Presence Felt on Opening Scoring Drive
metadata.description: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley got the start along with the rest of the team's first-unit offense during Thursday night's preseason opener, and he connected with quarterback Cam Ward on an 18-yard pass as part of the Titans' 11-play, 95-yard opening scoring drive. Ridley missed most of the 2025 season with a hamstring injury and a broken fibula, but his 925-yard pace across his five healthy games would have led the team by a significant margin. An overhauled receiver room featuring free agent acquisition Wan'Dale Robinson and fourth overall pick Carnell Tate adds significant target competition in 2026, but often going undrafted outside of deeper leagues, Ridley is a player to watch early in the season, as his versatility could still lead to usable fantasy contributions, even as the third option in what could be an ascending offense.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley Regains Weight After Stomach Virus
metadata.description: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley said he lost almost 15 pounds while dealing with a stomach virus but has since gained the weight back, according to Terry McCormick. Ridley also said he had eaten Chipotle before becoming ill, though the report did not identify the restaurant as the cause. The update is welcome after a quiet offseason in which Ridley's work was limited. His 2025 season ended after seven games because of a broken fibula and high ankle sprain, leaving him with 17 catches for 303 yards and no touchdowns. Tennessee added Wan'Dale Robinson in free agency and selected Carnell Tate fourth overall, giving Ridley more competition for targets this season. With the lost weight already restored, there is no indication in McCormick's report that the illness remains an active concern. Ridley's camp usage and role alongside Tennessee's new receivers are the more important fantasy developments to follow.

metadata.title: Calvin Ridley (illness) returns to practice Thursday
metadata.description: Calvin Ridley was back at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Ridley missed one day of practice due to an illness. His role in the Titans wide receiver room remains uncertain.
